name: Grab Holdings Limited
sector: Transportation / Southeast Asia super-app (mobility, deliveries, financial services)
moat_justification: Regional density leadership and super-app cross-sell are real but unproven in cash terms: ROIC (fundamentals.json roic_proxy) was negative for FY2021-24 (-29.9% / -17.9% / -9.9% / -3.5%) and only barely positive in FY2025 (+0.9%), users/drivers/merchants multi-home across GoTo, Sea/ShopeeFood and Foodpanda, and growth is shifting onto a credit balance sheet (lending book, Atome). Moderate moat, 5/10.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 3.3%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 20-F filer — per-share figures scaled x1.0 ordinary shares per ADS (Grab Holdings Limited Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-03-06), cover page: the securities registered under Section 12(b) are Class A Ordinary Shares (Nasdaq: GRAB) and warrants (Nasdaq: GRABW) — the Nasdaq listing is the ordinary share itself; no ADS class is registered and the company has no depositary/ADS program for the US listing (listing directories likewise carry GRAB as 'Class A Ordinary Shares', not an ADR)) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already

SHARES_FALLBACK: no diluted share count filed for 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022 — those history years use the basic / outstanding / dei count recorded in the shares_tag column; per-share history there is approximate
one_liner: Southeast Asia's leading super-app, moat 5/10 — Tier F on numbers: normalized owner's earnings are negative (-$0.06/share) because SBC ($241M in FY2025) exceeds what thin operating cash flow leaves after capex, so it clears no hurdle at $2.94 on filed OE; the bull case rests on adjusted-EBITDA growth (Q2 2026 +54% YoY, FY2026 guidance raised) converting into cash owner's earnings, which the filings have not yet shown.
moat_for: Density leader in Southeast Asia mobility + deliveries: record 54 million monthly transacting users in Q2 2026, on-demand GMV +21% YoY — local driver/merchant/user density across its markets
Super-app cross-sell: one account and wallet feeds mobility, deliveries, payments and lending, lowering the acquisition cost of each added service
Gross margin on the clean post-presentation-change years rose 36.5% (FY2023) to 42.0% (FY2024) to 43.2% (FY2025) per fundamentals.json — take-rate/pricing leverage as incentives normalize
Net-cash balance sheet: net debt -$1,380M at FY2025 (dcf_numbers.json) funds the fintech build-out without forced dilution
moat_against: ROIC has never covered the cost of capital in the filed history: roic_proxy -29.9% / -17.9% / -9.9% / -3.5% / +0.9% for FY2021-25 (fundamentals.json) — the franchise is still proving it earns its keep

Multi-homing everywhere: drivers, merchants and users split across GoTo, ShopeeFood/Sea and Foodpanda with near-zero switching costs; consumer and partner incentives were ~$706M in Q2 2026 alone (Q2 2026 results coverage)

Growth is being bought into credit: the scaling lending book and the Atome acquisition ($1.49B initial consideration, September 2026 announcement coverage) shift risk from marketplace take-rate to balance-sheet credit losses, and loan growth absorbs operating cash flow
SBC still consumes the cash engine: $241M in FY2025 against $79M of operating cash flow; share count growing 3.3%/yr (dcf_numbers.json)
Eight-country regulatory patchwork (gig-worker rules, banking licences, pricing) plus ASEAN FX headwinds the company puts at 2-3% inside FY2026 guidance
